The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for their discoveries concerning nucleoside base modifications that enabled the development of effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19. 
 [1]

Their groundbreaking work was crucial for developing mRNA vaccines rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Their discoveries fundamentally changed how scientists understand the interaction between mRNA and the immune system, allowing vaccines to be developed at an unprecedented pace during one of the greatest health threats of modern times.
